hazards.name: Space radiation
hazards.plain: Beyond Earth's magnetic field, high-energy particles pass through the spacecraft and your body. The dose adds up over the mission.
hazards.effects: Long-term cancer risk, possible effects on the brain, heart and immune system.

source.title: NASA Human Research Program: Hazards of human spaceflight

hazards.name: Isolation and confinement
hazards.plain: Months in a small space with the same few people, with little privacy and a fixed routine.
hazards.effects: Low mood, stress, poor sleep, slower thinking, team friction.

source.title: NASA Human Research Program: Hazards of human spaceflight

hazards.name: Distance from Earth
hazards.plain: Far from Earth, help is slow. Signals take up to 22 minutes each way, relay slots are scheduled, and during solar conjunction there is no contact for about two weeks. A reply from the flight surgeon can take weeks, so the crew must handle problems on board.
hazards.effects: Medical decisions happen on board with basic training; feeling cut off from family and ground support.

source.title: NASA Human Research Program: Hazards of human spaceflight

hazards.name: Altered gravity
hazards.plain: Weightlessness in transit, then one-third (Mars) or one-sixth (Moon) of Earth's gravity on the surface.
hazards.effects: Fluid shift to the head, heart and blood-vessel changes, bone and muscle loss, vision changes.

source.title: NASA Human Research Program: Hazards of human spaceflight

hazards.name: Hostile and closed environment
hazards.plain: Recycled air and water, noise, CO₂ build-up, microbes that change in space, and dust on the Moon or Mars.
hazards.effects: Headaches, poor sleep, infections, skin and breathing problems.

source.title: NASA Human Research Program: Hazards of human spaceflight
